_about: Contra (NES) best 1-player TAS (tasvideos 4623M, Mars608 & aiqiyou, 8:48.213, 31,745 frames, FCEUX 2.2.2, Contra (Japan)) measured section by section from its YouTube encode and compared with our AI's best verified US-ROM stage segments. Written 2026-10-16. See tas_compare.md for method and caveats. Every number carries a 'kind': measured (video or movie file), code (from the disassembly/ram_map or our RAM logs), or estimate.

sources.publication: https://tasvideos.org/4623M (links the YouTube encode 6kej45k7StE; obsoletes 4504M alex_ik 08:48.65)
sources.encode: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6kej45k7StE (960x720@60, AV1; 701.42 s incl. TASVideos card and the ending)
sources.ours: best verified US segments: S1 3898 (w37v3), S2 3604 (logs/s2/L2), S3 3494 (logs/s3/p2_var37), S4 5154 (logs/s4/T4r), S5 6039, S6 4028, S7 4407, S8 3237 (logs/s8/p2_var1); exits from chain1/run reports

encode_timing.evidence: Background scroll in stage 1 advances 1 px per video frame with a 2 px step every ~601 video frames (same in the archive.org MP4): the 60.0988 Hz picture was resampled to 60.000 fps by dropping one NES frame per ~601-608 video frames. The 7 intermission-skip Start presses of the movie (4084, 7291, 10407, 14995, 20801, 24584, 28745) each give a black frame at video v = 0.998356*n + 120.5 (residuals within +/-0.8; slope fitted 0.998337), so 1 video frame = 1.00165 NES frames and movie frame 0 = video ~120.5.
encode_timing.total_check: 31,745 movie frames map to video 120.5..31812; heart first explosion at video 31819 is 7 frames after the last input, as expected for a final bullet in flight
encode_timing.event_tolerance: +/-1 video frame for frame-exact visual events, +/-2 where the resampling drop falls nearby; approximate events carry tol

tas_inputs.start_presses: 150 (title), 395/398 (intro skip), 7 intermission skips (4084, 7291, 10407, 14995, 20801, 24584, 28745, each pressed twice 2-3 frames apart), 4 in-level 2-frame pauses: 22475-22477 and 22506-22508 (stage 6), 25964-25966 and 27563-27565 (stage 7)

S1.note: core red-flashing 3738-3739, explosion on the core 3740, wall-wide 3741

END_est.kind: estimate: heart explosion + 223 video frames (code-fixed chain, measured 223 on the record's video; assumed the same on JP)

per_stage.note: JP reaches the black 48 frames sooner after the explosion than US (416.7 vs 465): version or exit difference, not identified
JP reaches the black 41 frames sooner after the explosion than US (395.7 vs 437); our exit equals the record's, so most likely a version difference

per_stage_kinds: tas_* = measured video span x 1.00165 (NES frames, from the stage's first medal frame); ours_* = code/RAM rows from our logs (event seen = $3B + 3, medals seen on row 1); transitions = event to next stage's first medal frame

rooms.kind: TAS measured (barrier-gone onset, NES frames after the stage's medals); ours = room load + last-hit T + 34 - 1 (from the run reports)

stage3_climb.kind: measured (TAS video + movie), ours from logs/s3/p2_var37
stage3_climb.ours_waits: three long gaps of 96, 74 and 106 frames between jumps (rock platforms)

gameplay_ours.kind: code (sum of best verified stage results; not one chained run)

jp_minus_us_transitions.breakdown: about 202-205 per stage = the US 192-frame score screen + ~10 frames of US load/draw; stages 3 and 7 a further ~48 and ~41 frames shorter on JP before the black

tas_on_our_clock_jp.kind: measured start (first medal frame) + END estimated as heart explosion + 223

bottom_line.tas_check: TAS timing 31,745 = power-on->medals 449.2 (measured) + 31,524.8 - (END - last input = 229, computed) : consistent

ours_on_jp_est.kind: estimate = our gameplay + the TAS's JP transitions

tas_on_us_est.kind: estimate = TAS gameplay + our US transitions

ours_on_us.kind: code: sum of best verified segments (best complete verified run is chain1 = 34,474 = 9:33.622)
